input.overview: The marketing Header hardcodes “Sign in” and never reads the Flask session. After Google login the panel works because it calls `/api/auth/status`; home/pricing/MCP do not. Fetch that same endpoint on the client and swap the chrome to a signed-in identity + workspace link.
input.plan:
# Fix signed-in state on marketing pages

## What’s wrong

The panel and the marketing site share one Flask session cookie (`SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=Lax`, path `/`, same origin on kuchup.com). After Google OAuth, [`refreshAuth`](relocation_jobs/static/js/auth.js) calls `GET /api/auth/status` with `credentials: "same-origin"` and the panel shows the user.

The Next.js Header never does that. It always renders a static button:

```64:79:homepage/components/Header.tsx
          <Button
            as="a"
            href="/panel"
            variant="primary"
            className="hidden px-4 py-2 sm:inline-flex"
          >
            Sign in
          </Button>
```

[`homepage/app/layout.tsx`](homepage/app/layout.tsx) mounts this Header on every marketing route (`/`, `/pricing`, `/mcp`, `/how-it-works`, country pages). The homepage is a **static export** (`output: "export"`), so auth cannot be baked in at build time — it has to be a client fetch after load.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Browser
  participant Marketing as Marketing_Header
  participant Panel as Panel_JS
  participant API as Flask_api_auth_status
  Browser->>Panel: Google OAuth, session cookie set
  Panel->>API: GET /api/auth/status credentials same-origin
  API-->>Panel: authenticated true
  Browser->>Marketing: visit / or /pricing
  Note over Marketing: today: hardcoded Sign in
  Marketing->>API: GET /api/auth/status credentials same-origin
  API-->>Marketing: authenticated true
  Note over Marketing: after fix: Open workspace plus identity
```

No backend/cookie bug. Do not change [`relocation_jobs/core/auth.py`](relocation_jobs/core/auth.py) or OAuth.

## Signed-in UI (header)

Keep it smaller than the panel account menu (no credits/admin/sign-out on marketing). Sign-out stays in the panel.

- **Loading:** same-size reserved slot (`aria-busy`), not “Sign in”, so a signed-in user does not flash the wrong CTA.
- **Signed out:** primary “Sign in” → `/panel` (current flow).
- **Signed in:** compact initial + truncated email/username (same label as the panel: `email || username`) as a primary control → `/panel`, `title` = full label. Visible copy: **Open workspace**.

## Shared client pieces

Homepage already fetches public APIs from the browser ([`SearchResults.tsx`](homepage/components/SearchResults.tsx)). Add a small auth helper and hook in the same style:

- [`homepage/lib/auth.ts`](homepage/lib/auth.ts) — types + `fetchAuthStatus()` → `GET /api/auth/status` with `credentials: "same-origin"`. Treat network/non-OK as signed-out.
- [`homepage/hooks/useAuthStatus.ts`](homepage/hooks/useAuthStatus.ts) — `{ status: "loading" | "signedOut" | "signedIn", user }` via `useEffect`.
- [`homepage/components/AuthCta.tsx`](homepage/components/AuthCta.tsx) — client button used by Header and in-page “Sign in …” CTAs.

**Header:** collapse the duplicated sm/xs Sign-in buttons into one `AuthCta` with responsive classes.

**In-page CTAs** (same bug on other pages; they stay “Sign in …” even when the session exists):

- [`homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx`](homepage/app/pricing/page.tsx) — “Sign in with Google” / “Sign in for Free access”
- [`homepage/app/how-it-works/page.tsx`](homepage/app/how-it-works/page.tsx) — “Sign in to start tracking”
- [`homepage/app/mcp/page.tsx`](homepage/app/mcp/page.tsx) — “Sign in to the board”

When signed in, those become “Open workspace” / “Open the board” → `/panel`. AccessSection/CTA already say “Open the workspace” / “Open the board”; leave those.

## Deploy artifact

Flask serves the copied export from [`relocation_jobs/static/homepage/`](relocation_jobs/static/homepage/), not `homepage/` source. After TSX changes, run `npm run build:flask` in `homepage/` (or [`scripts/build_homepage.sh`](scripts/build_homepage.sh)) so the hashed `_next` chunks include the auth fetch.

No new pytest unless something backend-adjacent slips in. Existing `GET /api/auth/status` coverage already covers the session payload.

## Verify

- Signed out: Header still shows Sign in; `/panel` login still works.
- After sign-in, visit `/`, `/pricing`, `/mcp`, `/how-it-works`: Header shows identity + Open workspace, not Sign in.
- Hard refresh on `/` while signed in: brief reserved slot, then signed-in chrome (no sticky Sign in).
- Click Open workspace → panel still authenticated.
- Local: `PANEL_SCRAPE_ENABLED=1 python3 apps/panel/run.py` (5051) after the homepage rebuild.
